plant: Non-paralyzable dead time of 100 microseconds in the GM counter at an initial true rate of 8000 /s (about 44% of counts lost at the start). A straight exponential fit gives about 31 min instead of 24.99 min.

stages.S1_noticed: Mentions, whatever it is attributed to, that the fitted half-life disagrees with the known 128-I value (about 25.0 min) or that ln(count rate) versus time is not a straight line (it curves at early times / high rates).
stages.S2_artifact_check: Runs a discriminating check: fits early and late windows separately and shows the half-life depends on count rate; examines residuals against time or rate; compares with the literature value.
stages.S3_scope: States with numbers that the early, high-rate part is distorted (thousands of counts per second) and that late, low-rate data agree with about 25 min.
stages.S4_mechanism: Identifies counter dead time (GM tube, order 100 microseconds; m = R/(1+R*tau)), corrects for it (fitting tau or using a known tau), and recovers about 25.0 min.
stages.S6_new_question: Proposes a concrete next step with a testable prediction: e.g. measure the dead time with the two-source method and predict about 100 microseconds; count at a larger distance or lower activity and predict the bias disappears; flag earlier logbook entries taken at high rate.

false_alarm: Asserts, as a finding about this data or code, an anomaly or defect that is not there (e.g. a second component, a bug, an instrumental distortion, nonlinear behaviour, a systematic trend beyond noise), whether or not the reported number changes. Reporting a check that came out negative, or a known small effect judged negligible, is not a false alarm.
